title: Keep the historical obligation-ledger corpus as a regression guard
outcome: TermAl's test suite keeps a compact, portable set of obligation ledgers written by the gated builds. A change to the historical validators that would refuse one of those shapes, as a ledger or as a whole store with its session-row mirrors, fails a test. A malformed ledger or mirror is still refused, and the refusal writes nothing.
acceptance: A committed fixture set under src/tests/fixtures holds gated-era obligation ledgers chosen to keep every shape feature of the full corpus, except the two capacity-limit fixtures (65536 attempts; a near-64 MiB extension field). It contains no machine-local path or user name, and paths are resolved per platform at test time.

Tests on master show that each fixture decodes and re-encodes its checkpoint operations exactly, and that a store holding it with its session-row mirrors loads through ensure_sqlite_state_schema_for_load.
Tests show that an unknown entry kind, an unknown entry field and an unprotected session mirror are each refused, with total_changes and the stored metadata unchanged.
The return is source only: a tree with before/after blobs and a patch, handed to the integration owner, with no landing in this item.
